about: The fish genera's own presentation and ID marks, for every genus in play the IMR fish presentation gives no cues for (and marks for some it gives cues for, below), in every circle, the surprise cards' families aside (Pierre, 2026-11-08: each genus needs a short presentation and its ID cues, sourced, rules C2, C3, C6, before the genera open to more players; circles 2 and 3 since 2026-11-18, "d'abord le contenu"). Our own words, never copied, written from public sources: src, each {t, u}, t starting with the source's short name before its first comma. families: the families done, every family in play (each of its genera without IMR cues is in genera with a presentation, and with marks or in none with its reason; the build stops otherwise). genera, by genus name: plain, [one or two sentences on what the genus looks like and how it lives, its refs]; marks, 1 to 3 [visible feature that tells it from the other genera of its family, its refs], a ref being [src key, where in it (key couplet or species account, page)]. Only features seen on a photo: never a fin-ray, spine or scale count, nor a feature seen only in the hand; a species named is one of the genus's game species (rule C6). Most lines come from the FAO species identification guide for the Western Central Pacific (Carpenter and Niem, eds, vols 3 and 4, 1999, vols 5 and 6, 2001: each family's key to the genera, or its key to the species where it has none, and its species accounts), the rest from FishBase species pages; a genus the guide names otherwise says so (as Xyrichtys, as Pseudaluteres, as Dendrochirus brachypterus, as Apogon cyanosoma, as Trachinocephalus myops, as Dasyatis kuhlii, as Doryrhamphus (Dunckerocampus), as Carangoides bajad and C. ferdau, as Pseudochromis porphyreus). Circles 2 and 3, and a circle-1 genus with IMR cues (Dascyllus): where the guide splits the genera by counts only, or has no key, a visible feature that FishBase gives for the genus's only game species, or for each of its game species, stands as a mark (the sea slug cues' rule), a feature its species share rather than a tell-apart; the requiem sharks, whose FAO pages did not open, are from FishBase alone. Any circle, where neither gives a photo feature (Pierre, 2026-11-19: "Il faut sourcer tous les … qu'on peut"): a feature that Reef Life Survey (rls-), FishBase or Fishes of Australia (foa-) species pages give for each game species, or an FAO species catalogue (faocat-) for the genus, the ref's where then being the page's words verbatim, each checked by script against the page as read on 2026-11-19. The only genus of its family here gets a presentation only: the family's IMR cues and ID marks (tools/fish_sheets.json) tell it. none: a genus left without marks and why (no visible feature in the sources read): never a mark guessed. A genus with IMR cues may have 1 to 3 marks (no plain, never in none), from the same sources, faithful to its IMR cues and never contradicting them (rule C1; a source that differs goes to points.json, rule C5), shown under the IMR cues as a family's marks are (integrator's call on Pierre's "Mouais bof", 2026-11-19, to keeping them apart); one with no mark seen on a photo in the sources is simply left out. tools/build_fish.py add_families puts plain, marks, msrc and mby on fish.json genera; app.js fishGenera shows them on the genus card, learn.js genMarks on the sheet the genus opens.
